items.transcript: (A) Some armchairs are facing a window. (B) A curtain is being drawn across a window. (C) A seating area is illuminated by lamps. (D) Some magazines have been left on a table.
(A) They're viewing some paintings. (B) They're reading some brochures. (C) They're hanging some signs. (D) They're sorting some papers.
(A) The woman is turning on a lamp. (B) The woman is answering a telephone. (C) Folders are stacked on a chair. (D) There is a bulletin board above a desk.
(A) They're stacking some folders on a table. (B) They're looking at a whiteboard. (C) One of the men is typing on a laptop. (D) One of the men is lifting a mug.

Where can I pick up my conference badge? (A) It only takes a couple of minutes. (B) Yes, they're printing the badges now. (C) The greeter near the entrance can point you there.
Where did the owner decide to put the new outdoor seating area? (A) Right after the staff meeting. (B) Because customers kept requesting it. (C) Out along the west side.

Are you moving into the new apartment this Saturday, or waiting until the first of next month? (A) I found it through a coworker. (B) The ceremony was really moving. (C) My lease doesn't start until the first.
Would you like just one copy of this poster, or shall I make you two? (A) I'll just take a single, thanks. (B) The poster turned out really well. (C) Yes, sometime this afternoon.
When does the next dolphin show usually begin? (A) In about half an hour. (B) Just past the touch-tank area. (C) No, they're kept near the shore.
The dinner trays will be delivered before the guests sit down, right? (A) The trains run every twenty minutes. (B) There are forty guests on the list. (C) Yes, the van's arriving at six.
Honestly, I didn't expect Franklin's answers to be that impressive. (A) She answered on the first ring. (B) Sure, let's schedule another round. (C) Yes, and his examples were very specific too.
The extended warranty's included in this price, isn't it? (A) The meeting concluded right on time. (B) No, that's actually an extra charge. (C) They picked up the top prize.
What do we need to bring to the first painting class? (A) Isn't there a list on the sign-up page? (B) They're painting the hallway tomorrow. (C) Yes, she's a wonderful teacher.
Why don't we have lunch brought in so we can keep working? (A) Sure, that'd save us some time. (B) It was delicious, thanks. (C) At the restaurant across the street.

Did we decide to take the train or fly up to the regional office next week? (A) We really didn't want to risk any delays at the airport. (B) The regional office just finished a big renovation. (C) Let's train the new hires before that trip.
You haven't cleared the puzzle room between bookings yet, have you? (A) The puzzles are all pretty tricky. (B) Yes, it's clear outside now. (C) Was that on my list?
Should I close the blinds? (A) That one's stuck, too. (B) I'll turn the lights off instead. (C) The blueprints look fine.
Why don't we share a taxi to the trade show instead of waiting for the shuttle? (A) Because it needs a new chair. (B) It's just past the main station. (C) That works for me.
Haven't the microscopes been cleaned yet? (A) We took care of that yesterday afternoon. (B) Sure, I'd be glad to help. (C) They're pretty fragile, actually.
I've got a spare charger with me if your phone's running low. (A) This one's a bit larger, actually. (B) There's an outlet right behind you. (C) Thanks, but mine's still nearly full.
Why won't the dough mixer start up this morning? (A) The backup mixers are kept in the back room. (B) I ran into the same thing with mine last week. (C) Our morning shift starts at six.
When do advance tickets for the new film go on sale? (A) We sailed along the coast last month. (B) Not until this weekend, apparently. (C) Yes, right by the main entrance.
This afternoon's session is being recorded for later, isn't it? (A) It should finish around five. (B) She set a new sales record last month. (C) The audiovisual team would know.
Do you have a mallet I could borrow? (A) I lent mine to Owen. (B) How long did that last? (C) A few spare pegs, thanks.
You still haven't heard back from the fabric supplier about that delayed order, have you? (A) No, they haven't gotten back to us. (B) The dinner was quite delightful. (C) A bolt of gray wool.
Why are there so few cars in the parking lot this morning? (A) Aren't most people at the training session today? (B) Sure, whenever you're ready. (C) He's driving the new van today.
The dryers over there haven't finished the cycle yet, have they? (A) It's a dollar fifty per load. (B) Yes, they just stopped a minute ago. (C) No, I came on my bicycle.
Have you thought about switching to the digital menu boards? (A) Wouldn't that confuse our regular customers? (B) Yes, I got a little bored waiting. (C) The kitchen is right through there.
Shouldn't we lower the prices on these leftover shrubs? (A) Over by the back fence. (B) No, the manager has to approve that first. (C) The flowers look lovely today.

M1: Good morning, Northgate Radio. How can I help you? W1: Hi, this is Hannah Prescott. I entered your morning trivia contest yesterday, and someone called me last night to say I'd won. M1: Yes, congratulations! Your prize package includes two concert tickets, a thirty-dollar gift card, and one of our station T-shirts. W1: That's wonderful. How do I go about picking everything up? M1: I'd be happy to mail the package straight to your home. Or if you prefer, you can drop by our front desk any weekday afternoon.

M1: Hi, I bought two tickets for the seven o'clock showing tonight, but something's come up and we can't make it. Is it possible to change them to a later time? W1: Of course. Let me pull that up. Which film is it for, and what time would you like instead? M1: It's for the new adventure movie. If there's anything around nine, that would be great, as long as we can still sit together. W1: Let me check. Yes, the nine-fifteen screening has two seats side by side. There's just a small difference, though. The evening shows cost two dollars more per ticket, so that's four dollars in total. M1: That's fine. What do I need to do? W1: Just hand me your old tickets and step to the side, and I'll print the new ones for you in a moment.

M1: Good afternoon, welcome to Larkfield Portrait Studio. How can I help you today? W1: Hi. I'd like to book a family portrait session, ideally sometime this weekend. M1: Sure, we have openings both Saturday and Sunday morning. How many people will be in the photo? W1: There'll be four of us. It's for my parents' anniversary, so we'd like something a bit special. M1: Wonderful. We offer two packages. The standard one is a thirty-minute session with digital photos only. The premium one runs a full hour and includes a set of printed photos as well. W1: Let's go with the premium package. Oh, and how soon will the pictures be ready? M1: About a week for the prints. And one last thing — please arrive fifteen minutes early so we can go over the poses before we start.

M1: Good morning, I'm calling to confirm a group visit we booked at the Kentmere Museum. My name is Douglas Reeve, and I'm bringing my class this Thursday, the fourteenth. I just wanted to make sure everything is still in order. W1: Let me check for you. Yes, Mr. Reeve, I can see your booking right here for a group of thirty students on Thursday morning. Your visit also includes a guided tour of the main exhibit hall, and one of our staff members will meet your group at the entrance. M1: That's wonderful, thank you. One more thing—is there a place where they could eat their packed lunches after the tour? We'd like to stay a bit longer if there's space available.

M1: Thanks for calling Ridgeline Lawn and Garden. This is Trevor. How can I help you today? W1: Hi, I'd like to book an autumn leaf cleanup for my property. It's a corner lot with quite a few large maple trees in the back. M1: Sure, we can take care of that. I should mention, though, that we're very busy this season. The next regular opening is about three weeks out. W1: Three weeks? That's longer than I was hoping. Is there anything sooner available? M1: We do have weekend slots that open up faster, but there's an extra forty dollars for those. We also offer a three-visit autumn package. The per-visit rate is lower, and we could start next week. W1: Let me think it over before I decide. Could you email me the details for both options? I'll look through them tonight.

W1: Hi, Bradley. The customer survey results came in this morning — we've got responses from the last three months. One request came up over and over: people want more places to sit and read while they're browsing. M1: More seating? Camille, I agree it would be nice, but where would we possibly fit extra chairs? Every corner of the floor is already used for something. W1: You have a point — it is tight. What if we moved the new-releases table, though? It's sitting right by the front window, and that whole area could easily hold a couple of armchairs. M1: Hmm, that could actually work. We could shift the new-releases table over near the main aisle, where customers walk in first. It would probably draw even more attention there. W1: Good thinking. Let me put together a quick floor-plan sketch this afternoon and send it over to our store manager, Ms. Langley, for approval.

M1: Ms. Reyes, I finished drafting the agenda for next week's training workshop last night. I left a copy on your desk if you'd like to look it over this morning. W1: Oh, that's great — thanks for getting that done so quickly. The one thing we still haven't sorted out is who's going to present which part. The new hires are arriving on Monday, so we really need to lock that down. What are you thinking? M1: Well, I'd suggest you take the opening section on our company policies, since you've been running new-hire orientations for years and you know that material inside out. I can handle the software demonstration in the second half. It shouldn't add much to your plate — I only need about an hour today to pull my slides together.

M1: Hi there. My colleague and I are trying to use the projector in the conference room down the hall, but it just won't connect to our laptop. We've got a client presentation in about twenty minutes, so we're a little stuck. W1: Oh, that's a known issue with the older units on that floor — the connection port tends to fail. Rather than troubleshoot it now, why don't I lend you one of our spare loaner projectors? It'll connect right away. M1: That would be a lifesaver, thank you. Simon, does that work for you? M2: Absolutely. In the meantime, we can go back and get our slides loaded up and ready to run. W1: Perfect. Go ahead and head to the room — I'll bring the loaner over to conference room three and set it up for you in just a few minutes.

W1: Hi, come on in. Sorry about all the noise out front — we've got a crew taking down that old tree in the driveway this morning, so please just watch your step. M1: Not a problem at all. So, we're here to walk through the kitchen remodel, correct? I've put together some preliminary ideas based on the photos and measurements you sent over last week. W1: Wonderful. The two big things I really want are a lot more storage — I'm completely out of cabinet space — and a much bigger window above the sink. The one there now is far too small. M1: Both of those are definitely doable. The new window will take a little more planning because of the wall behind it, so let me bring in my colleague on that side. This is Ethan Beckett, our design consultant. M2: Nice to meet you. I've actually already put together three different window layouts for you. Let me pull them up on my tablet — you'll be able to see how each one would look from inside the room.

M1: Excuse me, could you tell me what time the penguin feeding starts today? W1: It's at two thirty. I should mention, though, that this week the feeding is being held at the South Gallery, not at the main viewing hall like usual. M1: Oh — the South Gallery? I already told my group to meet me at the main hall entrance. W1: That's right. The main viewing hall is closed for maintenance this week. Crews are upgrading the overhead lighting system, so all the feeding shows are running from the South Gallery until Friday. M1: I see. While I'm here, could I also book a spot on the behind-the-scenes tour this afternoon? W1: Certainly, we still have room — only two spots left, actually. Today's tour focuses on our sea turtle rehabilitation program, and it'll be led by Dr. Fowler, one of our biologists who just returned from a field research trip along the coast.

W1: Hi, a friend recommended Redbrook Tile Studio. I'm redoing the floor in my bathroom, and I'd like to buy some tile. There are so many options here — which one would work best for a bathroom? M1: For a bathroom, you'll really want something slip-resistant. The Slate Finish has a textured surface, so it won't get slippery when it's wet. That's the one I'd recommend. W1: Oh, that sounds perfect. I'll take enough boxes for the whole room, then. And once I've bought it, can someone come and put it in for me? W2: Yes, we offer a full installation service. I can have one of our teams come out this Thursday morning, if that works for you. W1: Thursday morning is great. Let's set that up. Thank you both so much.

M1: I'm setting up the kitchen in my new apartment, so I'm looking to buy a cookware set. The two things I really need are pans that are nonstick and pieces that are safe to put in the dishwasher. W1: All right, I can help with that. We have this chart comparing our four cookware sets. It shows which ones are nonstick, which ones are dishwasher-safe, and the price of each. What's the most you'd like to spend? M1: I'd rather not go over a hundred dollars. Hmm, looking at the chart, I see that two of the sets have both of the features I need, but one of them is above my limit. So I'll take the one that fits everything. W1: Great choice, that's a very popular set. Let me go and get one for you from the stockroom.

M1: Hi, I'd like to rent a private office here for my team. Is that something you can help me with at the front desk? W1: Absolutely. I can help you with that right now. First, how many people are on your team? M1: There are six of us. We actually just expanded — we started with four people last year, and business has been going really well. W1: Congratulations. Let me look at our list of private offices. We have one that comfortably fits a team of exactly six. You can see it here on the chart. M1: That sounds perfect. How soon could we move in? W1: The office is available at the start of next month. To reserve it, though, we'll need a security deposit from you today. M1: No problem. I can take care of the deposit right now. Thanks.

W: Good morning, and welcome to the Autumn Career Fair here at the Ridgemont Convention Center. We're delighted to have more than sixty companies taking part today, with company representatives ready to meet you and discuss their current job openings. At two o'clock this afternoon, a well-known career coach will give a talk on how to write a strong résumé. If you need help finding your way around the building, please stop by the information desk in the main lobby. We encourage everyone to pick up one of the free event guides there before you get started. We wish you the very best of luck today.

W: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for coming in. I wanted to go over the results of the customer satisfaction survey we finished collecting last week. The good news is that our customers rated our team's friendliness and product knowledge very highly, which is something we can all be proud of. However, only about fifteen percent said they were happy with how quickly we answer their calls, so that's clearly an area we need to improve. To help with that, the company has scheduled a one-hour training workshop next Thursday afternoon. Please add your name to the sign-up sheet by the door and make sure you attend.

W: It's time now for everyone's favorite part of the morning here on Sunrise Radio, our weekly listener giveaway. This week, one lucky listener will win a pair of tickets to the Brookmere Summer Music Festival, along with a backstage tour on opening night. To enter, all you have to do is call our studio line and tell us the name of your all-time favorite song, and honestly, it's as easy as that. We'll draw the winning name live on the air this Friday, so be sure you're tuned in. Coming up right after the break, we'll be chatting with local chef Adele Hoffman about her brand-new cookbook. Stay with us, and the best of luck to everyone!

W: Here's a quick reminder for residents about next week's waste and recycling collection right here in Ashgrove. Because Monday is a public holiday, every pickup will be shifted one day later than usual for the entire week, so your normal collection day simply moves back by one. Please have your bins out at the curb by seven A.M., because the trucks fill up quickly during these shorter weeks. For a full list of which materials each bin accepts, please visit our website at ashgrovecouncil.gov. That's all from the community desk.

W: As you all know, our bookstore has built up quite a loyal following over the years. Well, I'm happy to share that we've been chosen to host the city's children's book fair next month. This is wonderful news—it should bring plenty of new visitors through our doors and really boost our sales. To get ready, we'll be setting up an extra display table near the front window. Now, one more thing before we finish. I'd like each of you to suggest a few of your favorite titles for the fair, so please add your recommendations to the shared list posted in the break room.

W: Thanks for staying a few minutes after clock-in, everyone. As you all know, last weekend was the holiday rush, and we served roughly twice as many customers as we do on a normal Saturday and Sunday. I've been reading through the online comments customers posted about us, and the thing they mentioned most was how quickly we got their drinks out during the busiest hours. To thank you for that effort, I've booked the private room at Pinehurst Kitchen for the whole team this Friday at seven. It seats fifteen, so please let me know by Wednesday whether you can make it.

W: Hi, Ms. Lindqvist. This is Naomi Fielding calling from Clearline Internet. I'm just confirming your installation appointment for tomorrow morning; our technician should arrive sometime between eight and ten. Before he gets there, there are a couple of small things I'd like you to take care of. He'll need to get right up to the wall socket behind your living room sofa, so I hope that won't be a problem. Also, please remember that an adult over eighteen has to be home during the visit to sign for the new equipment. If tomorrow morning no longer works for you, just call our office back on this number, and we'll arrange another time.

W: Hi, this is Paula from Ashwood Auto Care, calling about your vehicle. The oil change and tire rotation you dropped off this morning are all finished up. However, during our inspection, the mechanic noticed that one of your brake pads is worn down much further than we would have expected. We can replace it for you today for an additional one hundred and eighty dollars, or you can pick up the car as planned and schedule the work for another visit. I would recommend taking care of it now for safety reasons, but I understand it wasn't part of what you originally budgeted for. Could you give me a call back as soon as you get this message and let me know how you'd like to proceed? If we hear from you by six o'clock, we can still finish the extra work today. That's when the shop closes, so please try to reach me before then.

M: All right, everyone, let's get started before the doors open. Tonight we have a large anniversary dinner, with just over two hundred guests expected in the main hall. I'd like all the tables fully set and ready to go by six o'clock sharp, so please check your stations now and let me know if you're missing anything. One important reminder: we have several guests who requested vegetarian meals, and those plates are marked separately, so make sure they reach the right seats. If anything changes during the evening, or if a guest has a special request, don't come looking for me — go straight to Lorna, who's handling all last-minute changes tonight. Her assignment is posted on the board by the kitchen door, so take a moment to see where she'll be stationed. Thanks, everyone, and let's make this a great evening.

W: Good morning, everyone. Now that the results of our user survey are in, I'd like to walk you through them. We ran the survey to learn which parts of our app people actually rely on, so we can decide where to focus our efforts. Please take a look at the chart on the screen. As expected, our messaging feature is by far the most popular, and the expense tool is also performing very well. But here is my concern. Sixteen percent of users told us they still depend on a feature we have barely touched in over a year. That's the one I want us to prioritize for our next update. So before Friday, please email me your individual suggestions for improving it.
